newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Countrywide Bank yr pretax rises.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Countrywide Bank yr pretax rises.

text.p: Countrywide Bank, the wholly-owned New Zealand unit of Britain's Bank of Scotland Plc, said on Thursday its pretax profit rose by 36 percent to NZ$82.8 million in the year to February 28.
In a statement the bank said its profit after tax was also up, rising 30 percent to $54 million, while return on equity rose to 20.3 percent from 17.7 percent.
Managing director David Wolfenden said that growth in assets by $864 million to $7.5 billion had contribued to Countrywide's cost/income ratio falling to 62 percent from 67 percent.
"As a result, in the last two years in particular, we have managed to increase both our market share and our efficiencies," Wolfenden said.
Countrywide's net lending rose by 15.2 percent to $6.2 billion while retail deposits were up 17 percent to $3.6 billion.
Residential lending of $5.1 billion gave the bank about 12 percent of the country's overall home mortgage market.
Countrywide was among the first lenders to cut loan rates after benign inflation data last week, but Wolfenden warned of concerns that government policy might undermine rate stability.
